correctness.rationale: Direct derivation in support-angle coordinates proves Jq=∫h(h+h″)(h²+h′²)^((q−2)/2), and exact first/second variations. Fourier Wirtinger bound for π-periodic variations gives uniform H1-coercivity for q<5; continuity of exact Hessian in C2 and homogeneity handle arbitrary directions and nearby base bodies. At q=5, symmetry cancels first variation, and exact trigonometric constant terms force F″(h_b)[cos2,cos2]=−6b+O(b²). For q>5 disk mode-two Hessian=(q−5)/2. The embedded checker reproduces exact Fourier certificates and numerical integral checks; numerical checks are not substituted for infinite-dimensional proof.

value.rationale: The local-versus-global dual Brunn–Minkowski distinction is mathematically motivated by the known global q=4 limit and the previously identified q=5 ball-point spectral threshold. The theorem specifies the exact C2-neighborhood threshold, settling the degenerate q=5 endpoint with an explicit two/four-harmonic resonance. It distinguishes all-neighbor concavity from single-ball stability and is not merely a numerical or renamed global inequality.
